hints.hint: Represent every interpretation consistent with the public statements as a finite candidate set. Group candidates by the value each speaker privately knows. Not knowing deletes groups whose relevant coordinate is already unique. Apply the announcements in chronological order, recomputing information sets after every deletion and never from the original set. The surviving candidate determines the requested quantity.
hints.subagent_summary: Execution 148.216 scored 2 of 8. Three failures hit the 16384-token cap; the finishing failures each fixed one reading of the public value, showed inside it that a speaker who knows their own number can compute the partner, called it contradictory, and then boxed a number from that same discarded reading. Both winners did the same thing but happened to land on the right value, so the training signal here is close to noise and does not indicate any missing step. Rounds 1-5, 7, 9 and 10 all added or swapped a clause at or above incumbent length and every one lost held-out, and round 8 showed that deleting the trailing original-set clause also costs held-out, so it is not inert. This proposal therefore changes no step and drops no clause: all six moves stay in the same order and meaning, with only redundant wording removed, 77 tokens down to 65.

hints.hint: Divide by the appropriate power of the variable and set w=(z-1)/z. The equation restricts w to a finite set on a circle. Solve the Möbius relation for z and characterize the image locus geometrically or by an x,y equation. Use all roots and check exceptional values before extracting the requested circle parameter.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts (148.217) scored 8/8 with zero ellipse/length-cap stalls, so no instruction is missing and no clause can be honestly cut: clause-tracing all eight shows each surviving element is used (divide by the power 3-11x, the w substitution 17-49x, w on a circle, inverting the Mobius relation 4-35x, an x,y equation 2-22x, all-roots 8/8, and 6/8 reason about an excluded/degenerate value). Every semantic variant has already lost for this hint: generalizing w=(z-1)/z (r6), replacing the geometric-or-xy fork (r7), deleting or swapping the exceptional-values clause (r8, r10), changing the closing verb (r9), and appending guards (r2, r4). The only untried lever is the one that won round 3 (81->70 tokens, J 3.00->3.25): a strictly lossless compression. 'by an equation in x and y' becomes 'by an x,y equation' - identical meaning, same six steps in the same order, 68 tokens versus 70.

hints.hint: Only a boxed value written after your reasoning block closes is graded, so a trace that never closes scores zero. Close the reasoning once one exact value has come out twice by two different routes. Then write the boxed value as the very first thing after closing, and put any explanation after the box, never before it, so being cut off costs nothing. Never restart the derivation in the write-up. Do not reopen a settled value; only a finished rival computation beats it, unease does not. Set up in coordinates first and write each object's extent; do not assume one figure sits inside another. If a rotation or offset stays free, ask whether the answer depends on it: a symmetry swapping congruent pieces makes every allowed value give the same result, so use the easiest one. For coverings, covered = sum of parts - overlap.
hints.subagent_summary: Rollouts scored 8/8; every one closed the reasoning block and boxed a value, so the output-protocol clauses are working. The remaining risk is the stop criterion: each trace reached the correct exact value by 6-16 percent of its budget, then re-derived it 26-51 more times, because 'one confirming check' names no condition that can ever be observed as satisfied, and prior rounds show truncation is this hint's main failure mode when the search drags on. This edit swaps that vague phrase for the concrete, checkable event the successful traces already produce - the same exact value arriving twice by two different routes - leaving every other clause byte-identical and the hint at exactly the incumbent's 169 tokens, so nothing the successes rely on is removed and no length tax is added.

hints.hint: When each term of a required linear pattern may come from any of finitely many fixed-degree polynomials fed consecutive integers, do not difference terms across different polynomials. Consecutive inputs make index and input interchangeable, so every value equals one shared affine L(x)=A+Bx of its own input. Group inputs by producing polynomial: each is a root of P(x)-L(x), which keeps P leading term and so has degree deg P. A nonzero polynomial of degree d has at most d roots, so a polynomial serves at most deg P inputs, one more forcing P=L. Sum that capacity over the whole menu for the total input count wanted, never one factor alone; attain it by letting each polynomial match L on its own block.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh round-11 rollouts (148.219) scored 5/8. The three failures all replace the per-polynomial capacity with a coefficient-counting heuristic instead of a root count: one asserts a degree-d polynomial 'passes through d+1 points because it has d+1 coefficients' and reports that, one caps a block at two inputs, one at one input and reports the menu size. Interpolation/determined-by language is dense in every failure and near-absent in the correct rollouts. The incumbent asserts the cap is deg P but never states WHY, so the student substitutes the wrong theorem. This edit inserts the one licensing fact - a nonzero degree-d polynomial has at most d roots - and is shorter than the incumbent (150 vs 153 tokens) with every prior step preserved.

hints.hint: Make each stated condition an equation; pin unknown constants first, then verify them in the original conditions, not your derived lines. Assume nothing unstated. Use the given relation to express remaining unknowns through one variable, then impose the defining equation. Reject roots outside the domain or repeating a known point. Box the first candidate meeting every condition.
hints.subagent_summary: Three of eight rollouts scored; four failures ended in finish_reason=length. Two died from one mechanism: after pinning the unknown constants they mis-cleared a fraction, then "verified" the result against their own derived linear equation instead of the given data, so a wrong parameter pair propagated and consumed the whole budget. The non-length failure obeyed every clause and even computed the target two ways, but had read one value off an inverse operator with a flipped sign that no self-consistent check could catch. So the incumbent's unattached "then verify" is made executable: verify pinned constants in the original stated conditions, not in your own derived lines. It is funded by cutting "a zero or impossible intermediate means relabel, not restart", which is inert - no rollout in rounds 6-11 ever relabels. Length stays at incumbent parity.

hints.hint: Treat relay-through-a-buffer tasks as stack shunting: fix one labeling, items bottom-to-top; keep ordered source, buffer, destination stacks; a run is a word of pushes and pops. Each item is pushed once, popped once: two moves per item, not one. Restate the target event as a condition on that word: a destination's bottom is whatever arrived first, its top whatever arrived last, so "lands at the bottom" constrains earliest moves, not latest. Never assume all n! orders or all words equally likely: stack rules leave many orders unreachable, forced moves make branches unequal; bare 1/k or 1/k! is a red flag. Multiply per-step probabilities along each admissible word: one where forced (empty buffer forces a push, empty source a pop), one half only at free steps; check branches sum to one.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 2/8. The one error all eight share is run length: every rollout sized a run as one move per item ("4 moves", 16 or 2^3 sequences) instead of a push plus a pop, and only one ever said an item moves twice. That single miscount produced every wrong answer (1/16, 1/2, 1/4, 1/24) and drove the four length-limit runs, which thrashed over reachability because their too-short words could not realize the event. The push/pop, labeling and arrived-first clauses are used 7-8/8, so nothing is cut; sum-to-one, unreachable and red-flag appear only 1/8 but rounds 6 and 7 lost held-out when those were removed, so they stay. The edit inserts one concrete counting fact early and pays for it by lossless rewording, landing at 176 tokens versus the incumbent's 177.

hints.hint: Numbers before symbols: set the huge parameter to 2, then 3, then 4, solve each tiny integer system by elimination, record the asked value. Divide consecutive entries, tracking signs separately; that ratio exposes the rule. Never build a polynomial in x or leave the table for theory. Confirm on one more size, then commit
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 0/8: all eight quoted the hint verbatim in the first paragraph and then built the polynomial-in-x model anyway; six hit the 16384-token cap with no boxed value, and the two that terminated reached the right factored structure but botched the final coefficient extraction. One rollout did compute two exact small-case entries by elimination, then declared the pattern 'not obvious' and abandoned the table for theory. Nine consecutive strategy edits to this hint have already lost held-out (rounds 6-10 tried replacing the ratio clause, the starting size, and the closing clause), so I did not attempt another. This is a strictly lossless compression: the two 'never' prohibitions are merged with 'or' and the terminal period dropped, keeping every step, meaning, and order intact at 68 tokens versus the incumbent's 70, which wins the length tie-break if held-out is unchanged.

hints.hint:
Write the quantity asked for as a formula in named symbols, including any unknown the text never states outright, usually a count; substitute numbers only at the end. Tag each given as a group total or a per-item amount.

If per-item amounts must be whole or equal, that unknown count divides every such total at once, so the candidates are the divisors of their gcd. A stated count describes a grouping; it constrains the unknown count without being it.

Make each percent or ratio a multiplier on the base it acts on, then rebuild each per-item amount and check it recovers its given total.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh round-11 rollouts scored 5/8. All eight computed the gcd of the stage totals and listed its divisors as candidate counts, so that machinery fires reliably, and all three failures were again the selection fork - a fork I tried to patch in rounds 2, 4, 6 and 7 and lost held-out every time, so I left it untouched. New evidence: not one of the eight ever rebuilt its per-item amounts from the count it picked, so the incumbent's closing 'check the result against every stated condition' is a vague gesture the student never executes. This edit replaces only that gesture with the same check stated as one concrete operation on numbers already written down, adding no rule, prohibition or tiebreak, and lands at 122 tokens versus 123.

hints.hint: For commuting same-degree polynomials, do not expand the full composition coefficient by coefficient; that exhausts your budget. Match leading and constant terms, then look for a shared symmetry. Strong ansatz: link the two maps by an affine involution, f = L(g) with L(t) = s - t, and require g(s - x) = s - g(x). That one reflection identity implies the commuting identity and collapses the unknowns to a single free parameter. Fix s from the given values at x = 0. Read the requested outputs straight from the symmetry relation rather than solving for every coefficient. Reflect the maps, not the argument x: substituting s - x into the given identity only reproduces it.
hints.subagent_summary: 7 of 8 rollouts died on the 16384-token cap with nothing boxed; the lone winner finished in 8k. The dominant, previously undiagnosed failure is that they applied the reflection to the argument instead of to the maps: they substituted s - x into p(q(x)) = q(p(x)) itself, which is a tautology, and then looped rediscovering that it gave no new information (one rollout said so 15 times) until the budget ran out. The winner tried that once, abandoned it for the map-level relation f = s - g, and solved it. Meanwhile no rollout this round mentioned a numeric verification, tried a different symmetry, or claimed no such polynomials exist, so the incumbent trailing clause is inert here and pays for the new line. Net 147 tokens versus the incumbent 152.

hints.hint: One application means the whole prescribed sequence of steps, never a single step; settle that first. On the smallest nontrivial instance with distinct labels, rewrite the whole state after every individual step, and after each finished application compare that state to the starting one; the count for that size is the first application that matches. A composite does not inherit the period of its parts. Get one more size the same way, fit one formula in the parameter, and box it, not rivals.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 2/8; five of six failures hit the 16384-token cap without ever boxing anything. The cause is corrupted per-application bookkeeping: they collapse an application's sub-steps onto one line, silently lose a swap, get a state that appears to return early, then thrash thousands of tokens re-deriving it (one concluded the period is 2 from a botched two-application run). Meanwhile the incumbent's 'build a table ... fill three rows' clause is inert - none of the eight rollouts wrote a table and none reached a third size. I cut that clause and spent the space on the concrete move they lack: rewrite the whole state after every individual step, and after each finished application compare it to the starting state, first match being the count. This is operation-agnostic and 5 tokens shorter than the incumbent.
